eip712_rules: digest = keccak256(0x1901 || domainSeparator || structHash); strings hashed with keccak256, uint fields 32-byte big-endian, address left-padded; the signature Orderly takes is 0x + r || s || v with v = 27/28. JSON messages: chainId, timestamps and nonces are numbers, Withdraw.amount is a string (raw USDC, 6 decimals), registrationNonce is the string the API returned.

request_rules.message: timestamp (ms, decimal) + METHOD + path including the query string + body ("" for GET and DELETE)
request_rules.signature: Ed25519 over the UTF-8 bytes of the message; header orderly-signature = base64url without padding
request_rules.body: contract-built JSON, no spaces; order keys: symbol, client_order_id (always the contract's g<request_id>, never the caller's), order_type, order_price (not for MARKET), order_quantity, side, reduce_only (only when true); prices and quantities are the canonical decimal digits written as bare JSON numbers
request_rules.validity: Orderly accepts a request for 300 s after its timestamp

requests.name: order with a quantity JavaScript would print as 1e-7
requests.note: the body carries the canonical digits 0.0000001, not JSON.stringify(1e-7) = "1e-7"; Orderly will refuse the size, the vector is about the bytes
